holidays.name: National Radio Day
holidays.description: A day to tune in and celebrate the humble radio, from crackly car stereos to late-night call-in shows. Fans are encouraged to dust off an old transistor and find a station they have never heard before.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States on August 20, a date linked to the first radio news broadcast, which aired from Detroit station 8MK (now WWJ) in 1920. Radio fans and broadcasters keep the tradition alive informally.
holidays.funFact: WWJ's 1920 election-night broadcast is often called the first commercial news radio program, and it reached only a few hundred homes with receivers.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Pecan Pie Day
holidays.description: A day for pie lovers to combine two great flavors in one gooey, nutty slice. Bakers and dessert fans mark it by making the pie or ordering it at diners.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that appears on American food-holiday calendars. Its exact founder is unclear, and it grew through food bloggers and bakeries sharing it online.
holidays.funFact: Pecan pie is often tied to the American South, and a common story says corn syrup recipes spread widely after corn syrup makers printed them on labels in the 20th century.

holidays.name: World Mosquito Day
holidays.description: A day that sounds like a joke but carries a serious message. It raises awareness about mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria and the science behind fighting them.
holidays.origin: Founded in 1897 when British doctor Sir Ronald Ross discovered that female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria to humans. He called it 'Mosquito Day' and it is still observed by health groups and scientists.
holidays.funFact: Only female mosquitoes bite, because they need the protein in blood to develop their eggs. Males feed on nectar.

holidays.name: International Day of Remembrance of and Tribute to the Victims of Terrorism
holidays.description: Not a quirky celebration but a solemn observance, included here as an official UN day that falls on a date known for odd holidays. It honors victims and survivors and encourages support for them.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2017, with the date set as August 21. Because it is observed right after August 20's mosquito and radio festivities, some calendars list the two days together.
holidays.funFact: This is one of the few UN days created specifically to center on the voices and needs of survivors and victims' families.

holidays.name: Hungary's St. Stephen's Day
holidays.description: Hungary's national day mixes fireworks, fresh bread blessings, and parades. The Danube lights up with one of Europe's biggest fireworks displays.
holidays.origin: It honors Stephen I, the first king of Hungary, crowned around 1000 AD. The day celebrates the founding of the Hungarian state and is also called the Feast of the New Bread.
holidays.funFact: The Holy Right Hand, the mummified hand of King Stephen, is carried in a procession through Budapest on the day.
